target_customer: Donors and researchers interested in human mind emulation; there is no paying customer segment
problem: Whole brain emulation is slow and underfunded. The foundation aims to fund and conduct research that accelerates human mind emulation and promotes a public manifesto.

founders.name: Dan Siroker
founders.role: Founder (listed as former founder on YC page)
previous_startups: Rewind AI (co-founder and CEO, per YC page and TechCrunch snippet)
founders.background_notes: GuideStar lists him as principal officer with a 2018 ruling year (search snippet).

competitors.name: Nectome
competitors.what: YC W18 startup preserving brains for possible future emulation, described by MIT Technology Review as a mind uploading service that is fatal to customers
competitors.funding_then: About $1M including $120K from YC and a $960K federal grant, per search snippets

technical_complexity.rationale: The stated goal of emulating a human connectome is research-grade and the foundation estimates mapping would only be feasible around 2084.

defensibility.rationale: A donation funded foundation has no product to protect; anyone can fund similar research.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent targeted the idea. Related groups such as Carboncopies Foundation exist as parallel nonprofits, not acquirers.

market_need_then: Interest in mind uploading was visible in March 2018 press coverage of Nectome, but no spending evidence exists for a donation model; a 2020 Hacker News thread drew skepticism per Gigazine.

identity.voice_and_tone: Philosophical and mission driven, with a three point public manifesto

branding.brand_signature: The Mind Emulation Manifesto that supporters can sign
branding.community_and_virality: Gigazine reported on the site in September 2020 after it drew attention on Hacker News.

brand_strength.rationale: Brief viral moment in 2020 but little sustained press; the descriptive name says what it does.

outcome_analysis: The foundation is listed as active on YC with a team of one, but no funding, results or growth are public. It appears to be a donation funded nonprofit founded by Dan Siroker around the time of YC Winter 2018, with a manifesto and a donation link as its main assets. It is not a venture outcome and success cannot be judged from the sources.
notes: YC page has no description and lists Siroker under former founders; the website names no founders, so the founder link rests on the YC page and a GuideStar snippet. Funding not public. Shyft and Bilarna pages describe it as a mental health tool and were treated as unreliable. Carboncopies Foundation is a separate nonprofit and is not listed as a dated competitor because no 2018 source was read. Nectome facts come from search result snippets of MIT Technology Review and Fortune; the MIT page itself was not opened.
